The 2026 United States Senate special election in Florida will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the United States Senate to represent the state of Florida. Republican appointee Ashley Moody and Democratic state representative Angie Nixon are the nominees for their respective parties. The winner will complete the term won in 2022 by Marco Rubio, who resigned in 2025 to become secretary of state.

After being appointed to the seat, Moody won the Republican nomination against minimal opposition. Alex Vindman, the former director of European Affairs for the National Security Council, was considered the Democratic frontrunner and held a significant fundraising advantage during the August 18 primary, but Nixon won the nomination with 56.1% of the vote in a major upset.

Democrats have not won a Senate race in Florida since 2012.

Background

[edit]

Marco Rubio, a U.S. senator from Florida since 2010, was announced as president-elect Donald Trump's nominee for secretary of state in November 2024.[1] He was confirmed by the Senate on January 20, 2025 in a 99-0 vote.[2] Ashley Moody, the attorney general of Florida, was named by Governor Ron DeSantis to fill Rubio's vacant Senate seat, and was sworn in the day after Rubio's confirmation.[3][4] Rubio's resignation triggered a special election for 2026, the next statewide election cycle in Florida. The victor of the special election will serve for the remainder of Rubio's term, until a regular election for a full term in 2028 is held.[5][6]

Democratic primary

[edit]

Campaign

[edit]

Angie Nixon, a progressive Democrat and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, won the nomination over Alex Vindman, despite Vindman having amassed $16.3 million in campaign funding compared to Nixon's $975,000.[35][36][37][38] Nixon campaigned on universal healthcare, free childcare, and a national rent freeze.[39] Nixon had criticized Vindman for having only recently moved to Florida; Vindman ignored her and attacked the Republican candidate, Moody.[35] The result was considered a major upset.[35][36]

General election

[edit]

Formerly a swing state, Florida has shifted increasingly to the Republican Party in recent elections.[97][98] A Democratic candidate has not won a Senate seat in Florida since 2012.[97][98][99] This will be the first U.S. Senate election in Florida in which both major party candidates are women.[100]
